items.title: Explicit Type Casting in Python
items.content:
Python will not automatically convert incompatible types. You must explicitly convert (cast) values using constructor functions:
- `int("42")` converts text `"42"` to integer `42`.
- `float("3.14")` converts text `"3.14"` to float `3.14`.
- `str(100)` converts integer `100` to text `"100"`.
- `bool(x)` converts any value to its truth value.
items.explanation: Type conversion transforms a value of one data type into another using explicit constructor functions.

10 (it rounds to the nearest whole integer)
items.correct_answer: 9 (it truncates/chops off the decimal part towards zero)
items.explanation: The `int()` function does NOT round numbers; it simply truncates (discards) the decimal portion.

items.explanation: `bool(string)` tests if the string is non-empty. Since `"False"` has 5 characters, it evaluates to True! Only empty string `bool("")` is False.
